messages:
zoe: Quick FYI - noticed behavioral mismatch between our RxJava and Coroutine Retrofit adapters on timeout+retry. Repro in samples/mobile/rx-vs-coroutines.zip.
marc: short summary? what differs?
zoe: Rx adapter will cancel underlying OkHttp call on timeout, but our coroutine adapter currently leaks the call and triggers OkHttp follow-up retries. On slow cellular this produces duplicate POSTs.
rachel: ack. Any logs?
zoe: snippet: 
```
W/Retrofit-Rx: timeout -> call canceled
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/event (single)
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/event (followup-retry)
```
marc: oh, that's bad. The coroutine adapter uses a custom dispatcher and uses call.enqueue + suspendCancellableCoroutine but we forgot to call call.cancel() on cancellation path in one branch. Rx path had disposal hooking fine.
rachel: fix idea: unify cancellation hooks between adapters and add a tiny parity test that exercises cancellation mid-request on emulator and asserts server saw only one attempt (or idempotency header).\o/marc: also consider making adapter-layer retry behavior explicit: either rely on OkHttp or make the adapter own retries. right now we have inconsistent policies.
zoe: agreed. For safety add idempotency header for non-idempotent endpoints in both adapters + add adapter-level config flag: prefer_okhttp_retries=true.
marc: I'll open WIP PR with: (1) add call.cancel() in suspendCancellableCoroutine cleanup, (2) add common CancelationSpec test between Rx and Coroutines, (3) document parity note.
ci-bot: queued: mobile-cancel-parity-smoke #211 (matrix: pixel-8:13). ETA ~10m :gear:
rachel: once merged we should cut patch and include in release notes under java/kotlin sdk parity bugfixes.
zoe: thanks, will attach small sample app and a short howto in devex/samples about testing cancellation parity.
